extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) guidance on examination of applications under the AIA amendments to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103, including applicability dates, prior art categories, exceptions, and procedures for overcoming rejections. Covers related topics such as claim interpretation, anticipation, obviousness, and evidence (affidavits/declarations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Applicability of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that the AIA changes to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 do not apply to applications filed before March 16, 2013 (pre-AIA applications) and describes circumstances that do or do not change an application's status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules: applications filed before 3/16/2013 remain governed by pre-AIA 102/103; filing an RCE or entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 does not create a new application for AIA purposes; submission of an amendment with new matter on/after 3/16/2013 does not alter pre-AIA status; a PCT filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before 3/16/2013 remains pre-AIA regardless of national stage date. See MPEP §§ 2131-2138 for pre-AIA prior art guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2150 Examination Guidelines for 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 as Amended by the First Inventor To File Provisions of the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview and detailed examination guidance implementing the AIA revisions to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (First Inventor To File framework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that AIA revised 102 and the standard to determine available prior art; references Public Law 112-29 and notes effective dates and cross-references to other MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2151 Overview of the Changes to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 in the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarizes the substantive statutory changes made by the AIA to prior art and obviousness provisions and how examination practice is affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level summary to orient examiners/practitioners to differences between pre-AIA and AIA provisions, including new prior art categories and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152 Detailed Discussion of AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance for applying AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) (what is prior art) and 102(b) (exceptions) during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaks down 102(a)(1)/(a)(2) prior art categories, timing, and exceptions; assists examiners in deciding which subsection applies and how to analyze disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.01 Effective Filing Date of the Claimed Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to determine the effective filing date of a claimed invention for purposes of applying AIA prior art rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains rules for priority/benefit claiming, how earlier filings affect effective date, and how effective filing date controls whether a reference is prior art under AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02 Prior Art Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) (Patented, Described in a Printed Publication, or in Public Use, on Sale, or Otherwise Available to the Public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains categories of public disclosures that qualify as prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections cover: (a) Patented, (b) Described in a Printed Publication, (c) In Public Use, (d) On Sale, (e) Otherwise Available to the Public, (f) No Requirement of 'By Others'. Provides factors for evaluating each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(a) - Patented
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when a patent (U.S. or foreign) qualifies as prior art under AIA 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses availability of patent disclosures and date-of-publication versus effective filing-date issues, and how to apply patents as references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(b) - Described in a Printed Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for treating a printed publication as prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses public accessibility, indexing, repositories, and determinative factors for whether a document is a 'printed publication'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(c) - In Public Use
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a public use under AIA 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains tests for public accessibility/use, circumstances that make an activity a public use, and evidence needed to support a public use rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(d) - On Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: How to determine whether an invention was 'on sale' and thus prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers sales, offers for sale, commercial exploitation, and relevant timing considerations under the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(e) - Otherwise Available to the Public
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch-all category for disclosures that made the invention available to the public under 102(a)(1) but do not neatly fit other labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides examiners to consider novel forms of public availability (e.g., online posting, demonstrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.02(f) - No Requirement of 'By Others'
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that AIA 102(a)(1) does not require disclosures be 'by others' — the statutory language differs from pre-AIA in this respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that inventor-originated public disclosures can be relevant prior art under certain AIA provisions and how that interacts with exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.03 Admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on treating admissions (statements by applicant/others) as prior art or evidence against novelty/claimability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when an applicant's own statements in the file/other documents can be used as a basis for rejection under AIA 102/103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.04 The Meaning of 'Disclosure'
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'disclosure' for purposes of prior art analysis under the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses what content and context constitute a disclosure that can be relied on against claims, including what must be described to be enabling or to anticipate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.05 Determining Whether To Apply 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for deciding whether a particular reference should be treated as 102(a)(1) (publicly available) or 102(a)(2) (U.S. patent documents effectively filed earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include effective filing dates, whether the reference is a U.S. patent/application, WIPO publication, and scope of disclosure available under each subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2152.06 Overcoming a 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on arguments, evidence, and procedures applicants may use to overcome AIA prior art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of affidavits/declarations, showing non-enablement, establishing earlier effective filing date, and asserting statutory exceptions. Cross-references 2155 for 37 CFR 1.130 affidavits/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2153 Prior Art Exceptions Under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes statutory exceptions that remove certain disclosures from the prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers inventor-originated disclosure exceptions and other limited exceptions under 102(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2153.01 Grace Period Inventor-Originated Disclosure Exception (102(b)(1)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the grace period exception where disclosures made by the inventor (or derived from the inventor) within a one-year window may be excepted from being prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details requirements to qualify for the inventor-originated disclosure exception and evidence needed to claim it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2153.02 Inventor-Originated Prior Public Disclosure Exception (102(b)(1)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers the exception for certain prior public disclosures by the inventor that would otherwise be prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains scope, timing, and limitations of this exception and how it differs from 102(b)(1)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2154 Provisions Pertaining to Subject Matter in a U.S. Patent or Application Effectively Filed Before the Effective Filing Date of the Claimed Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how U.S. patent documents and applications function as prior art under AIA 102(a)(2) and related exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses which subject matter is 'effectively filed,' how WIPO publications are treated, and interactions with common ownership or joint research agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2154.01 Prior Art Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) 'U.S. Patent Documents'
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes when subject matter in U.S. patents/applications (and certain published PCT/WIPO apps) is prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections include WIPO published applications, determining when subject matter was effectively filed, requirement of 'names another inventor', and treatment of copending U.S. applications as references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2154.02 Prior Art Exceptions Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2) to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes exceptions that can remove certain U.S. patent-document disclosures from being prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes inventor-originated disclosure exception, inventor-originated prior public disclosure exception, and common ownership/obligation-of-assignment exception (102(b)(2)(A)-(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2155 Use of Affidavits or Declarations Under 37 CFR 1.130 To Overcome Prior Art Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 can be used to rebut/explain prior art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers showing disclosure was by inventor or joint inventor, showing prior public disclosure by inventor, showing disclosure was made by another who obtained subject matter from the inventor, enablement issues, who may file an affidavit/declaration, and situations where 1.130 relief is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2156 Joint Research Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how joint research agreements affect prior art status, common ownership, and exceptions under the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains criteria for establishing agreements that disqualify certain references as prior art and procedures for examiners to assess evidence of such agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2157 Improper Naming of Inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive guidance on implications of incorrect inventor naming for prior art and examination under AIA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses corrective measures, when misnaming affects the status of a reference, and interplay with inventorship rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2158 AIA 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on applying the AIA version of 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses forming prima facie obviousness rejections under the AIA and references form paragraphs for 103 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2159 Applicability Date Provisions and Determining Whether an Application Is Subject to the First Inventor To File Provisions of the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains how to determine whether an application is governed by the AIA FITF provisions based on filing dates and claimed effective filing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for applications filed before/after March 16, 2013 and transition applications containing claimed inventions with mixed effective filing dates; includes required applicant statements for transition applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2141 Examination Guidelines for Determining Obviousness Under 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance on making and supporting obviousness rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 (principles, prima facie case, and factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scope/content of prior art, analogous art, differences between prior art and claimed invention, level of ordinary skill, suggestion/motivation to combine references, reasonable expectation of success, and considering all claim limitations and applicant rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2131 Anticipation — Application of 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on applying anticipation (novelty) principles under 35 U.S.C. 102 to determine whether claims are anticipated by prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of multiple-reference 102 rejections, genus-species issues, anticipation of ranges, and secondary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2111 Claim Interpretation; Broadest Reasonable Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for interpreting claim language during examination using the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses plain meaning, effect of preamble, transitional phrases, functional and nonfunctional descriptive material, and related claim construction considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2120 Rejection on Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and examples for making rejections based on prior art, including printed publications, patents, public use, and on-sale references under various statutory subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 2120.01 addresses rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and (a)(2) and pre-AIA 102(a),(b),(e); 2120.02 addresses knowledge by others/public use/on sale rejections. Provides procedural and substantive guidance for examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2161 Three Separate Requirements for Specification Under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, First Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the three distinct statutory requirements (written description, enablement, best mode) that the specification must meet under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an index to detailed guidance in MPEP §§2163-2165 on written description, enablement, and best mode requirements and examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2163 Guidelines for the Examination of Patent Applications Under the 35 U.S.C. 112(a) 'Written Description' Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for determining whether the specification provides adequate written description support for the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers support for claimed subject matter, standard for compliance, typical circumstances where issues arise, examiner burden, changes to claim scope, relationship to new matter, and amendments supported by original description.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2164 The Enablement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the enablement requirement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a): whether the specification enables a person skilled in the art to make and use the claimed invention as of the filing date without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes tests of enablement, undue experimentation factors, how to make/use the invention, working and prophetic examples, predictability, burden on the examiner, and enablement commensurate in scope with the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2165 The Best Mode Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains considerations for best mode under 35 U.S.C. 112(a), how it compares to enablement, and evidence/requirements for rejection for lack of best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses what constitutes concealment and examples of evidence of concealment; practical examination considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2171 Two Separate Requirements for Claims Under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, Second Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the distinct requirements for claims under 112(b): that claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention, and related claim-drafting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references MPEP §2173 for interpreting claims, definiteness, correspondence to the specification, and addressing specific claim-language issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2173 Claims Must Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim the Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for assessing whether claim language meets the statutory definiteness requirement and particularly points out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes interpreting claims, determining whether claim language is definite, correspondence between specification and claims, breadth vs indefiniteness, and many specific claim-language topics (antecedent basis, functional limitations, negative limitations, ranges, multiplicity, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2181 Identifying and Interpreting a 35 U.S.C. 112(f) Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when claim language invokes 112(f) (means-plus-function) treatment and how to interpret such limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to identify 112(f) claim elements, required structural support in the specification, and claim construction rules for means-plus-function claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2183 Making a Prima Facie Case of Equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for examiners on making a prima facie case that claimed subject matter is equivalent to prior art (doctrine of equivalents/equivalence arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes evidence and reasoning sufficient to establish a prima facie case of equivalence and related examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2184 Determining Whether an Applicant Has Met the Burden of Proving Nonequivalence After a Prima Facie Case Is Made
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for evaluating applicant evidence/arguments that assert non-equivalence following a prima facie equivalence showing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains types of evidence that can overcome a prima facie equivalence case and how examiners should analyze them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2190 Prosecution Laches and Res Judicata
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when prosecution laches or res judicata may bar patentability or affect examination and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses circumstances in which delay or prior decisions may impact the prosecution or enforceability of claims.
